cards.name: Section
cards.text: BID / SHOT COUNT / SCHEDULE

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Total shot count by complexity tier, crew-days estimated per department, client-approved budget and delivery schedule. Every later decision on this board gets measured against THIS document — scope creep is invisible until someone checks back here.

cards.name: Section
cards.text: ASSET PIPELINE — MODELING

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Hero assets vs. background/set-dressing assets, topology and poly budget per asset class, reference photogrammetry or LIDAR scan data if available, and modeling review status (blocked / in review / approved) per asset.

cards.name: Section
cards.text: ASSET PIPELINE — TEXTURING / LOOKDEV

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Texture resolution standard (4K hero, 2K background is typical), material library references, lookdev turntables pending supervisor sign-off, and any client-provided brand or material spec sheets that hero assets must match exactly.

cards.name: Section
cards.text: ASSET PIPELINE — RIGGING / ANIMATION

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Rig complexity per hero asset (how many controls, any facial rig), mocap or reference video for animated performances, and animation-supervisor review notes per shot — animation is usually the pipeline's tightest bottleneck, track it closer than anything else.

cards.name: Section
cards.text: LIGHTING & RENDERING

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Render engine and per-sequence settings, on-set HDRI/lighting reference for CG-to-plate matching, render-farm turnaround estimates, and the current AOV/render-pass checklist (beauty, diffuse, specular, cryptomatte for later comp control).

cards.name: Section
cards.text: COMPOSITING & DAILIES

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Daily notes from the comp supervisor, the shot-status board (WIP/review/approved/final), and any note that applies across the WHOLE sequence — broadcast those once here instead of repeating them shot-by-shot in review notes.

cards.name: Section
cards.text: VERSION CONTROL / PIPELINE TOOLS

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Naming convention for shot versions (e.g. SH010_comp_v014), where WIP files live (Shotgun/ftrack/Perforce/a shared drive), and any custom pipeline scripts the crew relies on — document the ONE script that would break the whole pipeline if the person who wrote it left.

cards.name: Section
cards.text: FINAL DELIVERY SPECS

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Full delivery spec sheet: codec, container, color space, delivery LUT, audio requirements (if any), and the QC checklist run before a show goes out — black frames, drop frames, and audio sync are the three things that get missed under deadline pressure.

cards.name: Section
cards.text: POST-MORTEM NOTES

cards.name: Note
cards.text: What actually worked, what didn't, and what changes for next time — written down here while the show is still fresh, since "we'll remember for next time" never actually survives to the next show.

cards.name: Section
cards.text: PLATES, LIDAR & LOOKDEV REFS

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Drop shot plates, on-set HDRI/lighting reference, LIDAR/photogrammetry scan previews, and lookdev turntable renders (image, video, or a real 3D model card — .usd/.usdz is the industry-standard interchange for exactly this). Hero-asset reference belongs here, not buried in a note.

connections.note: Approved bid/schedule sets the scope for modeling
Rigged/animated assets go into lighting and rendering
Approved comps go to final delivery
On-set HDRI/lighting reference feeds lookdev and lighting
Naming/versioning discipline underpins the highest-churn stage
Post-mortem findings feed the next bid’s estimates
